Abstract
We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.
IIntroduction
In the past few months, AI agents — by which we refer to a combination of a Large Language Model (LLM) and a harness that gives it access to tools — have developed the ability to perform a variety of scientific tasks with little or no human supervision. This impact is most visible in mathematics, where important open problems [1, 2, 3, 4], including the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize problem [5] and the “dying percolation conjecture” [6], have been solved by AI agents. In some cases, the agents were prompted by humans with no formal mathematical expertise themselves [7].So far, autonomous agents have had a less significant impact on theoretical physics and have not achieved a notable breakthrough. But they have rapidly become important in research. Experts have used agents in their research [8, 9, 10], and agents have autonomously solved mathematically well-defined problems [11]. Moreover, many researchers use agents to discuss ideas, perform calculations, search the literature and draft manuscripts. The objective of this paper is to scientifically evaluate one aspect of this progress at the current time — the ability of AI agents to solve well-posed and verifiable problems https://t.co/EP5Vyxeb88 this end, we present a suite of problems drawn from current research and sourced from world experts in a range of areas in theoretical physics. This collection does not include any important open research problems, since we advised potential contributors to prioritize direct publication of such results. The problems in our collection can be best thought of as “turn-the-crank” research problems, where known techniques are used to generalize an extant result. The result of each problem is, strictly speaking, novel, and sometimes even publishable, but not pathbreaking.All our problems have verifiable solutions, either in the form of a symbolic expression or a numerical answer that cannot be guessed. To the best of our knowledge, at the time of our evaluation, none of the answers to our problems were available publicly. However, we expect that solutions to some problems will appear in the literature in the near future, and one such solution (see §10A.10.1) was published after completion of the experiments described in this paper. Moreover, the problems do not meet a stricter criterion of being “untouched by AI.” In some cases, human experts used AI tools for assistance in solving the problems, and so we cannot rule out data leakage.Our problems are presented in Appendix A of this paper, and we strongly urge readers to glance over https://t.co/9aMmlPPGgp is nontrivial to construct problems that are relevant to research, are not significant in their own right, and have a solution that is verifiable, cannot be guessed, and is not publicly available. We asked experts to come up with the hardest possible problems in their respective areas. However, we did not reject problems merely because they were soluble by AI agents. Therefore, our evaluation suite aims to be representative of problems in theoretical physics, rather than an adversarial benchmark.We evaluated agents on two tracks, which we term the “isolated track” and the “realistic track.” These are distinguished by whether or not the agent is allowed to access the https://t.co/nWR3whP2AI our experiments we found that, in the realistic track, GPT-6-Astra with Codex (Astra) achieved a near-perfect accuracy of 98%, and both Astra and Opus 5.5 with Claude Code CLI (Opus) achieved an accuracy of 92% in the isolated track. The average change in accuracy for most agents between the two tracks was quite small. Since many of our problems rely on formulas from the literature, this indicates that leading LLMs have effectively memorized large parts of the theoretical physics literature.Our results indicate that some frontier models may have already surpassed the best human researchers in their ability to perform concrete calculations, even in specialized topics. This is a significant milestone, with implications for education and research in theoretical physics.The ability to solve concrete problems has traditionally been highly valued in theoretical physics. Problem solving is central to physics education [12, 13]. Students are evaluated through high school competitions such as the International Physics Olympiad [14], examinations used in graduate admissions [15], and graduate qualifying exams [16].However, problem-solving abilities are only one of the skills that theoretical physicists require. The main aim of the field is to construct theories of the physical world. Second, it is necessary to ask the “right” high-level questions of the theory. Third, it is necessary to convert these questions into concrete calculations. Therefore, it is only at a late stage in the scientific process that one is faced with a concrete calculation with a verifiable https://t.co/1uLp8Cg9ct a corollary, the excellence of AI agents at problem solving does not immediately imply their all-round excellence at autonomous physics research. Human experts are required in the loop. Autonomous excellence at research might emerge in the near future but will require more than problem-solving ability.We hope that the assessment presented in this paper will aid discussions in the theoretical physics community on the evolution of pedagogical and research practices. Similar discussions are underway in the mathematical community [17, 18]. It is desirable for the theoretical physics community to have these discussions in advance, before AI has a significantly disruptive impact.Several agents included in this study do not yet saturate our evaluation. For example, among open-weight models, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek) harnessed in Codex scored 54% and 50% on the realistic and isolated tracks, respectively. We hope that our collection of problems will be useful for model developers. It might serve as a method of measuring the abilities of agents to assist theoretical physicists in their research.
I.1Previous work
There has been considerable previous work on benchmarking the abilities of LLMs on school [19, 20], competition [21, 22], and undergraduate physics [23]. Benchmarks such as TPBench [24], SciCode [25], FrontierScience [26], PRL-Bench [27], QMBench [28] and notably CritPt [29] include research-level problems in addition to simpler problems. Our paper adds to this literature but is distinguished by its exclusive focus on modern research-level problems. Our evaluation methods are also different since most other evaluations do not usually allow agents to access the full range of tools that they would have access to in the real world.Terminal-Bench-Science [30] is broader in its coverage than this assessment, which is focused on theoretical physics and provides deeper coverage within that field. Moreover, since we seek to evaluate agents on realistic problems that physicists would encounter, we do not discard problems simply because they can be solved by agents.Our evaluation is roughly comparable to the “First Proof” challenge in mathematics [31, 32, 33, 34] in the sense that it involves unpublished research-level problems. However, while First Proof involves human assessment of proofs, our evaluation is automated and only based on the final answers.This paper is organized as follows. In Section II we explain the class of problems included in our collection. In Section III we describe the procedure used to evaluate agents on this collection. In Section IV, we provide a summary of the quantitative and qualitative conclusions of our evaluation. We conclude with some discussion in Section V. The appendices provide details. In particular, Appendix A contains a full list of our https://t.co/MUif8XQFUX 1:Three example problems and their expected solution trajectories.
(a)Black-string Page time.
Example problemConsider a black-string background with two branes at equal angles, π/10, from the vertical in AdS4. By comparing minimal surfaces that extend from the defect to the brane to minimal surfaces that extend from a defect on one side of the horizon to the other, find the Page time for this configuration in units where the temperature is 1/(2​π).Expected answer flow Step 1: Locate arXiv:2012.04671 [35] that discusses a similar problem in AdS5. Step 4: Analyze the extracted field and compute the length scales required.
IIProblems
The problems in our collection were obtained by soliciting world experts from different areas of theoretical physics.We asked experts to contribute problems that met the following three criteria.
1.Problems related to current physics research;
2.A known solution that was simple to verify but difficult to guess;
3.A solution that could not be looked up in the published literature or elsewhere.We also requested that contributors not publish their solutions in the near future, to avoid contamination of the evaluation.These criteria are quite restrictive. In particular, they exclude problems from ongoing research that the experts intended to publish in the near https://t.co/rgAYXsqvDZ pathway for contributors to satisfy these criteria was to give us a problem from their research notes that they had worked out but not taken the trouble to publish.A more common alternative was for contributors to adapt a problem solved in one of their recent papers. By changing some parameters in a physics calculation, it is often possible to obtain a new problem with an answer that cannot be guessed from the old answer. Problem contributors could solve such a problem by modifying their existing code or calculations. But another expert human, or an AI agent, would need to locate and understand the original solution; reconstruct the calculation in detail; and then adapt it to the modified problem.Such an exercise is often assigned to graduate students who are starting research, since it helps them survey the literature and master the relevant techniques. This method is also sometimes used by researchers to write “incremental papers.”Therefore, none of the problems in our dataset constitute breakthrough open problems. Solving them does not require great originality or the ability to construct new physical theories. However, it does require familiarity with current research, and the ability to understand and accurately adapt cutting-edge calculational techniques.
II.1Example problems
Box 1a shows an example of such a problem and the expected solution trajectory. The problem statement there is closely related to a problem solved in a paper that appeared on the hep-th arXiv [35]. The statement of the problem is deliberately terse and it requires a deep understanding of recent developments in holography to decipher the statement.A human attempting this problem would presumably start by locating this paper. This would help them understand the terms and the scope of the problem. The setup of [35] involved a five-dimensional spacetime, and the next step would be to generalize the equations there to a four-dimensional spacetime as asked in the problem. This is a straightforward step but requires some care.The resulting equations cannot be solved analytically. They give rise to a singular boundary-value problem. One must solve the equations in a series expansion near the singular points and then use a “shooting” routine [37] to obtain the full solution.When presented as above, the individual steps in the solution might seem straightforward. However, the solution requires several components including a familiarity with the relevant literature and also a familiarity with numerical techniques. This might require the human to provide hints to the agent, or perhaps provide the agent with the high-level algorithm above. But specialists in the area of one of these problems are unlikely to be familiar with the terminology of the other two problems. As many of you know, over the past two years I’ve shifted my research from foundation models and NLP into AI-native chip design. What I’ve found: the problems feel 10x harder than software engineering. Writing functionally correct RTL is only the beginning.

As models saturate on benchmarks like CVDP and ChipBench, I keep coming back to one question: how far can AI go toward designing a complete chip on its own?

Today, we’re thrilled to introduce Build-A-Chip-Bench, the industry’s first AI benchmark for end-to-end chip design, built by ChipAgents in collaboration with @NVIDIA. It tests whether AI can take a design from specification all the way to verified GDS.

The top model scored just 16.6%.

Today’s models can produce functionally correct RTL in some cases, but reliably meeting physical requirements remains a major challenge. We still have a long way to go, and that’s what makes this research so exciting to me.

Proud of our research team and grateful to our industry partners for helping us give the community an honest measure of where we are and how much work lies ahead.

1 AM Top-of-the-Hour News

President Trump announced plans for a new defense "super range" in Montana. The president during a rally stop in Kalispell to support GOP candidates:: “I'm pleased to inform you and announce that right here in Montana, the Department of War is going to establish a new super range for testing advanced weapons and tech technologies including potential autonomous weapons, space and electronic warfare technology, supersonics and hypersonics. ”
The range would be in addition to the Montana Spaceport & Test Range and the affiliate Limestone Hills Innovation & Test Campus.

The Department of Homeland Security is rejecting a recommendation that would automatically turn on body cameras worn by ICE agents.: “According to the Government Accountability Office, the agency declined to have cameras start recording when agents draw their weapons or when nearby officers activate their own cameras. Instead, DHS will stick with its current policy requiring agents to manually turn on their cameras during arrests, searches, and similar operations. The watchdog agency had recommended automatic activation to help ensure encounters are recorded and improve accountability. Stacy Lynn, Worldwide News Network, Washington. ”

Hundreds of U.S. troops are reportedly being sent to Latin America to fight against drug cartels. NewsNation's Blake Burman has more: “The New York Times reporting that roughly 600 troops will be deployed to Panama before then heading to Colombia and Honduras. The military also planning to create a new Western Hemisphere military command that will be stationed in Miami. ”
The soldiers will reportedly train and conduct joint exercises with regional forces.

Stocks fell to their worst day since July. The S&P 500 was down 87 for its fifth loss in the six days since hitting an all-time high. The Dow Jones lost 49, and the nasdaq slipped 512 points.
A report that shows inflation accelerated last month increasing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting.

Former Venezuela president Nicolas Maduro and his wife are expected in a New York courtroom today. They are facing a rewritten indictment that accuses them of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured victims, including 3 Americans.
Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores are expected to plead not guilty to the charges added to a drug trafficking indictment brought against them. They were seized from their home in Caracas by the U.S. military in a January raid.

Costa Rica has inaugurated a high-security prison as part of a crackdown on organized crime and drug trafficking.
The $35-million facility can hold 5,100 inmates and is intended for the country's most dangerous criminals. Costa Rica's President Laura Fernandez says "Those who break the law must pay for it," also promising to respect prisoners' fundamental rights.

A new report says that the world's climate has reached a dangerous threshold...: “The 7th annual State of the Climate report was released by the journal Bioscience on Wednesday. Greenhouse gasses such as carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide all reached record levels this year, according to the study, which looked at data from 16 indicators of climate change, including carbon levels and ocean temperature changes. The study says that efforts to reduce dependency on carbon and fossil fuels can help stem the trend, but those efforts and others need to move more quickly to have an impact, Bill Rakoff, Worldwide News Network. ”

TODAY'S WORLD NEWS
Wednesday, October 14, 2026 | Comprehensive Global News Report
A World Confronting War, Economic Pressure, Political Division, and Technological Transformation
Executive Summary
The international situation on October 14, 2026, is dominated by several interconnected developments: escalating Middle Eastern hostilities, continuing warfare in Ukraine, rising inflation, intensifying competition between China and Western economies, and rapid advances in artificial intelligence.
The most consequential breaking development involves the Strait of Hormuz, where reports of attacks and a sunken commercial vessel have raised fresh fears for international shipping and energy supplies. In the United States, unexpectedly strong inflation figures are adding pressure to financial markets and policymakers just weeks before the November 3 congressional elections.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's dependence on satellite communications has become a renewed security concern, European leaders are considering stronger trade defenses against China, and international health authorities are responding to a major Ebola outbreak in Central Africa.
Several encouraging developments also deserve attention, including progress in medical technology, expanded renewable electricity generation, and international efforts to improve pandemic preparedness.
Reporting standard: This report draws on reporting attributed to Reuters, the Associated Press, international institutions, and scientific and medical sources. Battlefield allegations, government claims, economic forecasts, and early research findings should be distinguished from independently established facts. The original report's October 14 breaking-news claims have not been independently reverified in this text-only edition.

1. Middle East: The Strait of Hormuz Becomes a Major International Flashpoint
A commercial shipping emergency
On October 14, the Associated Press reportedly said that Iran had announced a cargo ship had sunk after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Guardian separately reported attacks against commercial vessels in the area, including vessels struck by missiles. These reports point to an increasingly dangerous maritime environment, although details of individual incidents, responsibility, and the total number of vessels affected require careful confirmation.
The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the wider Indian Ocean.
Its importance extends far beyond the Middle East. It is one of the world's most strategically important petroleum shipping passages, and disruptions can affect fuel prices, shipping insurance, international trade, and inflation.
Why this conflict matters globally
The immediate danger is not limited to the ships themselves. Every significant attack introduces additional uncertainty into international energy markets.
Possible consequences include higher transportation costs, fuel shortages in vulnerable importing countries, increased maritime insurance premiums, and further military escalation.
The conflict also complicates diplomacy involving the United States, Iran, Israel, and regional governments.
Earlier international mediation efforts involved Pakistan and Qatar, which described progress toward a peace framework during June discussions. That diplomatic history demonstrates that negotiations have been pursued, although it does not establish that a durable settlement has been achieved.
Outlook: The critical questions are whether shipping attacks continue, whether maritime security can be restored, and whether diplomatic negotiations can prevent further escalation. None of those outcomes is assured.

2. Yemen: Hospitals Overwhelmed as Fighting Intensifies
A separate but closely connected humanitarian emergency is unfolding in Yemen.
Reuters reportedly stated October 14 that renewed fighting between the Houthis and forces supporting Yemen's internationally recognized government had overwhelmed medical facilities and disrupted assistance to approximately 800,000 people.
The escalation has affected Taiz, Marib, and areas near the Red Sea coast.
Key reported developments include more than 200,000 people displaced in recent weeks, shortages of essential medical equipment and supplies, and hospitals struggling to treat large numbers of wounded civilians and combatants.
Saudi Arabia also faces growing insecurity
Reuters separately reported attacks affecting civilian travel and Muslim pilgrims in Saudi Arabia, including a deadly strike at Riyadh's airport.
Yemen's conflict has deep roots in political fragmentation, regional rivalry, economic collapse, and years of military intervention. The broader confrontation involving Iran and the United States has intensified the pressures surrounding it.
Humanitarian organizations emphasize that medical supplies alone cannot address the crisis. Safe transportation routes, protection for civilians, and reliable access for food and medicine are also essential.
Humanitarian significance: The greatest immediate concern is that interrupted medical care, displacement, and insufficient food supplies will lead to further preventable suffering even outside active combat zones.

3. Russia–Ukraine War: Satellite Communications and Military Support Under Pressure
Ukraine faces new technological restrictions
The Associated Press reportedly stated October 14 that restrictions affecting Starlink satellite communications had slowed some Ukrainian drone operations.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed concern about the restrictions and difficulties obtaining advance intelligence regarding Russian strikes.
Ukraine continues to rely heavily on satellite connectivity, drones, air-defense systems, and international military assistance.
These technologies have become essential to modern warfare. They support battlefield communications, reconnaissance, command systems, and remotely operated equipment.
Russian attacks and European assistance
Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure remain a serious problem, particularly when energy systems are targeted.
Zelenskyy traveled to Britain seeking further assistance, including accelerated delivery of air-defense equipment.
Ukraine has reported some territorial advances in the east, while Russian attacks continue. Such battlefield claims should be distinguished from independently verified territorial changes.
China's role in military supply chains
An October 13 Associated Press investigation highlighted another vulnerability: Ukrainian manufacturers remain dependent on some Chinese-produced drone components.
Ukraine has reduced its dependence substantially, with the report estimating the Chinese share of component sourcing declined from about 90% in 2024 to 28% in 2026.
However, certain sensors, electronic components, and specialty materials remain difficult to replace.
Threats to Black Sea shipping
Bulgaria also reported drone attacks affecting commercial shipping in the Black Sea and suggested Russia was likely responsible, while acknowledging that definitive attribution had not been established.
The combined developments illustrate how the war extends beyond ground combat to shipping, infrastructure, global manufacturing, satellite technology, and Europe's security arrangements.
Outlook: Important uncertainties include the durability of Western support, availability of air-defense systems, future Russian military operations, and whether diplomatic negotiations can produce an enforceable ceasefire.

4. United States: Inflation Surges Ahead of Congressional Elections
September inflation reaches 3.7%
New economic figures reportedly published October 14 show that annual U.S. consumer-price inflation reached 3.7% in September, rising from 3.4% in August.
The increase was heavily influenced by energy prices.
Reported year-over-year changes include:
CategoryReported annual increase
Overall consumer prices3.7%
Gasoline34%
Fuel oil74%
Air travel22.4%
Core consumer prices2.6%
The core measure excludes food and energy.
These figures reflect national price-index changes and should not be interpreted as every household experiencing precisely those increases.
Why prices remain under pressure
Several factors may be contributing simultaneously.
Higher energy costs raise transportation and production expenses. Disruptions in international shipping can further increase the cost of imported goods. Strong investment in technology infrastructure may also affect demand for electricity, construction capacity, and equipment.
However, assigning a precise percentage of inflation to any single cause would require additional economic analysis.
Financial markets react
Reuters reportedly stated that the inflation figures contributed to a significant sell-off in artificial-intelligence-related stocks.
Among the companies affected were CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle, and Dell Technologies.
The Nasdaq reportedly declined approximately 2% during the sell-off, while long-term government borrowing costs increased.
Higher borrowing rates matter because they can influence mortgages, business investment, government financing costs, and company valuations.
The Federal Reserve's dilemma
The Federal Reserve must balance inflation control against economic growth and employment.
Market expectations shifted toward the possibility of an interest-rate increase at the October 27–28 monetary policy meeting, but market probabilities are not official policy decisions.
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's forthcoming comments at the International Monetary Fund meetings are receiving close scrutiny.
For ordinary households, the central question remains whether wages and retirement income can keep pace with the cost of living.

5. U.S. Politics: November 3 Midterm Elections Approach
The United States is less than three weeks away from its November 3, 2026, congressional elections.
Control of Congress will influence the Trump administration's ability to advance legislation, secure funding, and navigate congressional investigations.
President Trump's campaign activity
The Associated Press reportedly stated that President Donald Trump has been campaigning for Republican candidates across several Western states, emphasizing gun rights, energy development, and his administration's policies.
His campaign appearances have also addressed controversy surrounding a luxury aircraft provided by Qatar for possible presidential use.
Republicans are seeking to protect congressional seats, while Democrats are campaigning on economic conditions, government oversight, abortion rights, and other policy disagreements.
Supreme Court decision affecting campaign advertising
On October 14, Reuters reportedly stated that the U.S. Supreme Court sided with Republicans in a procedural dispute involving Federal Communications Commission rules on political advertising rates.
The ruling concerns whether political party committees may receive advertising price advantages traditionally associated with candidates. It also involves when challenges to agency decisions can be pursued in court.
Because campaign advertising can influence voter outreach, the dispute has practical consequences during the final weeks before the election.
Federal Reserve independence becomes another political issue
Lawyers representing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook challenged the fairness of a White House inquiry concerning allegations that she has denied.
The dispute raises broader questions about due process and central-bank independence. The existence of allegations does not establish wrongdoing.
Outlook: The election results could substantially affect U.S. fiscal priorities, immigration legislation, energy policy, foreign assistance, and oversight of the executive branch. The eventual outcome remains uncertain.

6. Global Economy: IMF Warns of Uneven Growth and Mounting Debt
World financial leaders meet in Bangkok
The International Monetary Fund and World Bank are holding their 2026 annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.
The central question is whether the global economy can maintain growth while facing major military conflicts, expensive energy, rising government borrowing costs, and potentially disruptive technological changes.
The IMF's October 13 economic outlook reportedly projects:
Economic indicatorForecast
2026 global growth3.1%
2027 global growth3.4%
2026 global inflation4.7%
These are estimates and forecasts, not final annual outcomes.
The IMF emphasizes that growth is increasingly uneven.
Countries benefiting from the artificial-intelligence investment boom are generally performing better than many energy-importing and lower-income economies.
Government debt becomes a worldwide concern
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has urged major economies, including the United States, to address mounting public debt.
High borrowing costs can force governments to devote more revenue to interest payments instead of infrastructure, education, health care, or social services.
The Associated Press reportedly stated that U.S. federal debt has exceeded $40 trillion, adding urgency to discussions about long-term fiscal sustainability.
There are competing policy perspectives. Some economists favor tighter fiscal discipline to stabilize debt, while others warn that aggressive spending reductions could damage growth or essential public services.
The best approach depends partly on a country's economic conditions, debt structure, and ability to raise revenue.
A new global inequality initiative
Reuters reportedly stated October 14 that Barbados had joined an international coalition seeking the creation of a United Nations-backed panel addressing economic inequality.
Countries involved include Spain, Brazil, South Africa, Germany, and Japan.
The initiative reflects concern that wealthier nations may capture a disproportionate share of the economic benefits created by advanced technology.
Outlook: Global economic growth remains positive, according to IMF projections, but energy prices, government debt, and the possibility of financial-market corrections present significant risks.

7. China and Europe: A Growing Battle Over Manufacturing and Trade
China's exports rise sharply
Reuters reportedly stated that China's September exports increased 36.3% from a year earlier, while imports grew 31%.
China recorded a September trade surplus of approximately $133.5 billion, bringing its cumulative surplus over the first nine months of 2026 to roughly $938 billion.
The figures demonstrate China's continued industrial strength despite concerns about its domestic property market and consumer demand.
Semiconductors, vehicles, and technology-related products contributed to the export expansion.
European leaders consider stronger protections
European Union leaders are debating measures to protect manufacturing industries against competition from Chinese imports.
Reuters reported an EU-China trade deficit of approximately €360 billion in 2025, with further imbalances emerging in 2026.
The political dilemma is substantial.
European manufacturers argue that domestic industries need protection against unfair competition and market distortions. Others caution that import restrictions can raise consumer prices, provoke retaliation, and disrupt supply chains.
Taiwan warns about economic dependence
Taiwan's Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung warned European governments against excessive dependence on Chinese suppliers.
He argued that close economic dependence could create geopolitical vulnerabilities and encouraged stronger economic relations between Taiwan and Europe.
China, which claims Taiwan as part of its territory, opposes diplomatic initiatives that appear to strengthen Taiwan's independent international standing.
Global significance: This debate affects automobile manufacturing, semiconductor production, critical minerals, defense technology, and future trade relationships.

8. Global Food Security: Fertilizer Disruptions Threaten Agriculture
One of the less-publicized consequences of the Middle Eastern conflict is its potential effect on worldwide fertilizer supplies.
Reuters reportedly stated October 14 that a United Nations official warned of a possible food-security crisis unless arrangements can be made to transport essential fertilizer products through the Strait of Hormuz.
Before the severe disruption, the shipping route carried approximately one-third of globally traded urea and nearly half of seaborne sulfur, according to the report.
Both materials are important to agricultural production.
Farmers who cannot obtain sufficient fertilizer at workable prices may reduce applications, switch crops, or experience lower yields.
The most vulnerable countries are often those that rely heavily on imported agricultural inputs and have limited financial resources.
A UN-supported transportation proposal includes maritime coordination through Oman.
Important distinction: A large-scale food crisis is a warning about what could happen if disruption persists, not a confirmed prediction that particular countries will experience famine.

9. Global Health: Ebola Outbreak Demands International Attention
Major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
The World Health Organization is monitoring a serious outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
According to figures attributed to WHO through October 12:
Reported indicatorFigure
Confirmed cases in DRC9,066
Confirmed deaths in DRC4,361
Reported case fatality ratio48%
These reported surveillance figures require verification against the relevant WHO bulletin and may be revised.
The outbreak is described as concentrated in eastern Congo, particularly Ituri and North Kivu.
A laboratory-confirmed imported case was also reportedly identified in Kenya after travel through Uganda. The previous report stated that the patient died October 5.
Why controlling Ebola is difficult
Ebola spreads through direct contact with infected bodily fluids or contaminated materials, rather than through ordinary casual airborne transmission.
Effective outbreak response requires rapid identification of infections, appropriate isolation, medical care, contact tracing, safe burial practices, and community cooperation.
Access is particularly challenging in areas affected by insecurity or damaged health systems.
The reported case fatality ratio describes confirmed cases within this outbreak. It does not mean every infected person has precisely that probability of dying, and it can change as surveillance improves.
Progress in pandemic preparedness
On October 12, WHO reportedly announced renewed international commitments concerning pandemic prevention and efforts to detect future outbreaks within 24 hours.
These initiatives aim to improve surveillance, laboratory coordination, and international response capacity.
They represent meaningful public-health efforts, although implementation and financing will determine their effectiveness.

10. Medical Breakthroughs: AI Could Make Implanted Devices More Responsive
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania have reportedly developed an experimental artificial-intelligence platform allowing patients to communicate more directly with medical devices.
Reporting published October 14 described work featured in Nature Medicine, initially focused on epilepsy.
The system is designed to allow patients to receive personalized information from implanted devices, report symptoms, and potentially improve communication with clinicians.
Potential future applications
Researchers envision possible applications involving cardiac monitoring devices, insulin pumps, and treatments for certain neurological conditions.
For example, future systems could help patients better understand device alerts or communicate symptoms to their medical teams.
However, experimental capability is not the same as proven clinical benefit.
Before wider adoption, such technologies require careful evaluation of safety, accuracy, privacy, cybersecurity, and the risk of incorrect recommendations.
Patients should not assume that existing implanted devices possess these AI capabilities.
The larger significance
The most promising direction is technology that helps clinicians and patients understand medical information more quickly.
Artificial intelligence may improve communication and monitoring, but it must complement rather than replace qualified medical judgment.

11. Climate and Environment: Warnings Increase Alongside Clean-Energy Progress
A new assessment of Earth's vital signs
A report discussed in the Washington Post on October 14 examined major indicators of environmental change.
Published in BioScience, the research identified continuing concerns involving greenhouse-gas concentrations, rising ocean temperatures, wildfires, and diminishing polar ice.
The analysis reported record concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide, alongside continuing pressure from fossil-fuel use.
These findings are consistent with the established scientific conclusion that human activities, primarily greenhouse-gas emissions, are driving long-term global warming.
Individual extreme-weather events require separate attribution studies to determine the influence of climate change on their likelihood or intensity.
Encouraging energy developments
The same report highlighted substantial progress in low-carbon electricity.
Approximately 43% of global electricity generation in 2025 reportedly came from low-carbon sources, including renewable and nuclear power.
Renewable electricity generation also reportedly surpassed coal in the global energy comparison, while electric-vehicle adoption continued expanding.
These improvements demonstrate that energy systems are changing, even though global emissions remain a serious concern.
AI helps cities respond to dangerous heat
Researchers and technology companies are using AI to identify neighborhoods with especially high heat exposure.
Google's Heat Resilience work has reportedly expanded to more than 50 cities, according to reporting published October 14.
Yet identifying a vulnerable neighborhood does not automatically protect residents. Cities still need effective interventions such as shade, cooling centers, emergency communication, and accessible medical services.
Outlook: Climate risks are expected to remain substantial, while practical progress will depend on emissions reductions, infrastructure investment, and adaptation measures.

12. Artificial Intelligence: Economic Opportunity and Financial Risk
Artificial intelligence is simultaneously supporting global economic growth and creating new uncertainty.
The IMF considers technology investment an important reason that the world economy has remained relatively resilient despite military conflicts and high energy costs.
Where the benefits are emerging
AI is supporting investment in data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, cloud computing, scientific research, and industrial automation.
Countries that manufacture advanced electronics or provide infrastructure for AI systems are benefiting from increased demand.
In health care, AI applications are being investigated for medical imaging, research, diagnosis support, and analysis of biological information.
Where the risks are emerging
Companies developing AI infrastructure face substantial capital costs.
Large facilities require electricity, cooling, advanced chips, networking equipment, and considerable financing.
Reuters reportedly stated October 14 that inflation concerns and rising borrowing costs triggered sharp share-price declines among several AI-related companies.
These movements do not establish that AI investment as a whole is failing. They demonstrate that investors are reassessing whether projected future earnings justify current costs and valuations.
The employment question
Artificial intelligence may transform work in administration, customer service, research, programming, finance, and other fields.
The IMF has warned that significant portions of employment in advanced economies could be exposed to AI-driven changes.
Exposure, however, does not necessarily mean complete job replacement. Some occupations may be augmented rather than eliminated.
The long-term effects will depend on technological capabilities, workplace adoption, education, government policy, and the creation of new occupations.

13. Other Humanitarian and Diplomatic Developments
Gaza and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict
The humanitarian consequences of the Israel–Hamas war remain a major international concern.
Medical care, reconstruction, civilian protection, displacement, and the future political administration of Gaza continue to shape the international debate.
An additional diplomatic development reportedly occurred October 14 when Colombia opened an embassy in Jerusalem after restoring relations with Israel.

「仕事ができるけど性格に難がある人」を、エースとして重宝する会社は危ない。

営業成績はトップ。専門知識も豊富。難しい案件も解決できる。だから多少の問題行動には目をつぶる。

「あの人は仕事ができるから」
「成果を出しているから仕方ない」
「代わりがいないから強く言えない」

こうして、職場に特別扱いされる人が生まれる。

会議で他人を見下す。後輩のミスを必要以上に責める。気に入らない相手には協力しない。自分の機嫌で周囲を振り回す。

それでも数字さえ出していれば高く評価される。

ここで考えてほしい。

その人が生み出している成果は、周囲に与えている損失を上回っているのだろうか。

本人が1億円の売上をつくっていても、その人のせいで優秀な社員が辞めていく。若手が萎縮して挑戦しなくなる。周囲が余計な気遣いや調整に時間を奪われる。

そうした損失は、決算書のどこにも直接は表れない。

だから経営者や管理職は、目に見える成果ばかりを評価してしまう。

さらに厄介なのは、こういう人が管理職に昇進することだ。

個人として成果を出せるのだから、チームを率いても成果を出せるはず。そんな安易な判断で、人を動かす立場に就けてしまう。

結果、部下は疲弊し、組織の雰囲気は悪化する。それでも本人は数字を出しているから、上層部からの評価は高い。

そして、まともな人から辞めていく。

もちろん、成果を出す人を正当に評価することは重要だ。性格が合わないという理由だけで、優秀な人を排除すべきでもない。

ただし、他人への敬意を欠き、周囲の力を奪う行動まで、成果を理由に許してはいけない。

本当に優秀な人とは、自分一人で大きな成果を出す人だけではない。

周囲の力を引き出し、組織全体の成果を高められる人でもある。

100の成果を出していても、周囲に150の損失を与えているなら、その人はエースではない。組織にとってマイナスの存在だ。

会社が最も警戒すべきなのは、仕事ができない社員だけではない。

成果を出しているという理由で、何をしても許される社員をつくってしまうことだ。

そして、その特別扱いを決めているのは、ほかでもない経営者や管理職自身なのだ。

北京 43岁的IDG资本高管，姓顾，圈内人都叫他顾总。

没人知道，他跟自己的嫂子已经偷偷好了四年。

事情败露，竟然是因为顾总在办公室打飞机。

那天晚上，他正看着嫂子发来的私密视频自慰，妻子突然推门进来，当场撞见。

顾总吓得裤子都没提好。

妻子没哭没闹，三个月后，两人和平离婚。

顾总以为终于能跟嫂子双宿双飞，先后给她转了600万。

没想到钱刚到账，嫂子就提出分手。

顾总气得找到大哥。

大哥却笑了：

“你睡我老婆四年，我拿你600万，不过分吧？”

原来大哥早就知道两人的奸情。

更离谱的是，那600万被大哥拿去投资了一家AI公司。

公司叫SeekDeep AI，创始人外号“娘子”，一个40岁的中年码农。

三年前，娘子曾找顾总融资。

顾总只看了十分钟，就把人赶走了。

“40岁还在写代码，能有什么前途？”

如今SeekDeep AI估值60亿，大哥那笔投资账面价值涨到了4000多万。

顾总气得准备起诉。

没想到前妻突然宣布再婚。

新郎竟然是娘子。

原来前妻经营花店时，曾借给娘子20万创业。

离婚后，又拿着分到的300万投资了SeekDeep AI。

如今股权账面价值超过5000万。

顾总彻底崩溃。

直到有天，他无意中看到一份早期股东名单。

发现大哥名下的股份，竟然有一半属于前妻。

他这才明白，妻子当年撞见自己打飞机，根本不是偶然。

那天晚上，是大哥故意让嫂子发的视频。

妻子早就知道他出轨，只是在等他露出破绽。

顾总不甘心，找到娘子质问。

娘子却笑了：

“顾总，你可能忘了，十年前我就在你投资的公司写代码。”

“当年嫌我35岁还在写代码，把我裁掉的人，就是你。”

顾总愣住了。

十年前，他嫌娘子年龄大，把人裁了。

三年前，他嫌娘子没前途，拒绝投资。

如今自己因为一场婚外情，间接给娘子的公司送去了600万。

老婆嫁给了娘子，嫂子回到了大哥身边。

只有他，房子没了，老婆没了，600万也没了。

最讽刺的是，顾总后来才知道：

当年那个办公室的门，根本不是妻子忘了敲。

而是嫂子提前告诉了妻子，他晚上一定会一个人留在公司。

别人打飞机，最多浪费几张纸。

顾总打了一次飞机，却把自己打成了前妻新丈夫的天使投资人。

你说，这场无间道里，顾总到底输给了女人，还是输给了那个被自己裁掉的中年码农？

《美股公司深度解析21：$CRWD CrowdStrike究竟是一家什么公司？为什么我认为网络安全可能是AI时代最值得长期研究的软件赛道之一？》

很多投资者研究AI，只关注算力、芯片和云计算，却忽略了一个问题：当全球企业把越来越多的核心数据、业务系统和AI代理接入互联网，谁来保护这些资产？这就是网络安全公司的机会，而$CRWD CrowdStrike正是这个领域的重要企业之一。它不是传统意义上销售杀毒软件的公司，而是通过Falcon云原生安全平台，为企业提供终端安全、云安全、身份保护、威胁检测和安全运营等服务。公司主要采用SaaS订阅模式，客户按使用的安全模块和服务持续付费。相比一次性销售软件，这种模式能够带来更稳定的经常性收入，也让企业有机会不断提高单个客户的消费金额。

先看财报。2027财年第二季度，也就是截至2026年7月31日的季度，CrowdStrike营收达到14.71亿美元，同比增长26%，其中订阅收入14亿美元，占总营收约95%。更值得关注的是ARR年度经常性收入达到58.4亿美元，同比增长25%，当季新增ARR约3.33亿美元，同比增长51%。Non-GAAP营业利润3.72亿美元，调整后营业利润率约25%，自由现金流3.77亿美元。但必须注意，公司GAAP营业亏损仍有3323万美元，GAAP净利润仅约530万美元。调整后利润与真实会计利润存在明显差距，其中一个重要原因就是股权激励及相关税费，当季达到约3.99亿美元。因此研究CrowdStrike，不能只看ARR和调整后利润，还必须关注普通股股东最终获得多少实际收益。

真正的护城河来自Falcon平台的安全数据、威胁检测能力和产品整合。大型企业的IT系统极其复杂，需要同时保护员工设备、服务器、云环境和身份权限。CrowdStrike通过统一平台提供多种安全模块，能够降低客户管理不同安全产品的复杂程度。截至第二季度末，51%的订阅客户已经采用至少6个模块。客户部署的模块越多，迁移至竞争平台的成本通常也越高。未来增长主要来自云安全、身份安全、下一代SIEM，以及AI代理安全。尤其是AI代理，当企业允许AI自动调用系统、读取文件甚至执行任务后，安全问题就不再只是防止病毒入侵，还包括防止权限滥用、敏感数据泄露和恶意指令。今年9月，CrowdStrike进一步扩大与OpenAI及谷歌云的合作，正是为了争夺这部分市场。

财务方面，公司第二季度末持有约50.1亿美元现金，资产负债表拥有较强流动性。管理层预计2027财年全年营收达到59.91亿—60.11亿美元，第三季度营收约15.23亿—15.29亿美元。不过竞争同样激烈，微软$MSFT、Palo Alto Networks $PANW、Fortinet $FTNT都在扩大网络安全产品覆盖。CrowdStrike还必须面对2024年全球Windows系统故障事件带来的长期信任和法律风险。估值方面，截至10月9日，$CRWD收于275.04美元，市值约2822亿美元，滚动市销率超过52倍。由于GAAP利润规模仍然很小，传统PE已经缺乏实际分析价值。技术面短期关注260—265美元区域的承接，以及280—287美元附近能否有效突破。

我的观点是，CrowdStrike拥有非常优秀的商业模式，但当前估值已经反映了极其乐观的增长预期。网络安全是企业越来越难以削减的支出，AI普及又会进一步扩大潜在市场。不过好行业不代表所有股票都便宜，尤其当一家企业已经获得超过50倍营收的估值时，未来几个季度不仅需要保持收入增长，还必须持续提高利润率、自由现金流和每股盈利。

我长期看好网络安全行业，但对$CRWD的判断是：公司质量很高，当前估值同样很高。未来决定股价上限的，不是AI时代会出现多少网络攻击，而是CrowdStrike能够把多少安全需求转化为真正属于股东的持续利润。

records.text:
Gartnerが「80％以上のネオクラウドが消滅する」と衝撃の予測を発表。

ロジックはシンプルで、AIインフラへの投資規模（2026年に約1兆ドル、2027〜2030年に追加約6兆ドル規模）に対し、AI関連の収益が追いつかないという観点。

資本コストや12%のROICをカバーするのに必要な累計収益は約8.5兆ドルなのに、実際に見込めるAI収益は3.5〜3.6兆ドル程度という試算を出している。結果として大規模な減損（3.5兆ドル超）と市場の極端な集約が進む、という見立てである。 

GartnerのアナリストWill Sommerは下記のように語る。

「資産が消えるわけではない。独立運営をやめるというのは、買収・提携・完全な破綻を含む。消える会社すべてが失敗するわけではない。」

潰れた／独立できなくなったネオクラウドのデータセンターはどうなるか。
現実的なシナリオは買収が主流。

財務健全性が高く巨大なキャッシュフローを持つネオクラウドやハイパースケーラー（Microsoft、Amazon、Google、Metaなど）、プライベートエクイティ、インフラファンドが、潰れそうな資産や会社をディスカウント価格で買う。物理的なデータセンター、電力契約、冷却設備、土地は価値があり、AI自体の需要は旺盛であるため放置されるケースは少ないと考えられる。

また、運営権を引き継ぐステップインも考えられる。
CoreWeaveなどの多くは、顧客契約を担保にしたSPV（特別目的会社）で資金調達している。OpenAIやMicrosoft、Metaなどがそのステップイン権（運営を引き継ぐ権利）を持っているケースがあり、事業者が倒れても容量自体は継続利用されやすい構造である。

さらに、ネオクラウドが破綻してしまった場合は債権者が資産を押さえ、GPUやデータセンターを売却することになる。GPUは減価が速いが、建物・電力接続権・立地は確実に残るのでAI需要者には極めて魅力的な資産となる。

最後に、建設予定地の扱いだが、資金調達が難しくなった弱いプレイヤーのプロジェクトは遅延・中止・譲渡になりやすい。すでにIPOや債務調達の枠が閉じつつある動きが出ている。直近ではFirmusなどのIPOが投資家の需要不足で断念された。電力を確保できているサイトは特に人気で、強靭な資本を持つ主体が引き継ぐことになる。

つまりどういうことか、分かりますね？

・売上高は610億9900万円（前年同期比1.1%増）📈 会社予想に対する進捗率（達成率）は99.7%と、ほぼ予想通りの着地です！ゴルフのキャディバッグやトレッキング用品、ワールドカップ効果でサッカー用品が好調に推移してトップラインを牽引しました⚽️✨

・来期（2027年8月期）の通期予想は、売上高613億円（0.3%増）、営業利益3億円（3.4%増）、最終利益5000万円の黒字転換を見込んでいます🎯 配当も年間26円をキープ予定で、株主還元への姿勢は崩していません💰✨

・キャッシュフローを見ると、営業CFは2億2900万円のプラス、投資CFは設備投資などで12億1900万円のマイナス💸 財務CFは長期借入金の増加などで35億8300万円のプラスとなり、手元の現金残高は62億8500万円へ大幅に増えています🏦 自己資本比率は39.7%に低下しましたが、資金繰りはしっかり固めている印象です🛡️

【まとめ】

一時的な特損で赤字の沼にハマりましたが、ECと物流の最適化という次へのステップに向けた足場固めのフェーズです🔥 今後の巻き返しに要チェックですね！

records.text:
本日ストックボイスにて
堀古英司さんのお話😊
（まとめてあります）

（CPI重荷に？）
・ヘッドラインが出て、マーケットがびっくりした。
・債券市場を見ると、10年債は最近でいちばん高い金利水準を一度トライしたものの、本当に一瞬で戻り、引けは前日より利回りが低い。
・にもかかわらず株は戻っていない。
・ですので、私は、10月の投資信託の決算を控えた需給、、、特有の動きじゃないかと思っています。

（SOX4%下げ、行き過ぎ？）
・もともと変動率の大きい指標です。
・今年おそらく投資信託でいちばん損が出ているのが、長期の債券で、最近は売られてもすぐ戻ってくるのを見ると、もう相当投げ終わったんじゃないかと、、、含み損はもう実現した。
・その損に充てる利益のほうは、やはりSOX指数のような半導体銘柄が多いでしょうから、需給で損に充てる銘柄としてそのあたりが売られているのかなという気がします。
・今日の動きが今後の流れを決定づけるとは捉えないほうがいいと思います。

（10月決算を控えた要因？）
・タイミング的に引き続き需給が悪いので、材料さえつけば売られやすい時期です。
・材料は「中国が安い半導体を開発した」だの、「新しいものを作った」だの、何でもいい。
・もともと需給が悪くて、売られた後にみんなが「中国がー」と言い出すパターンなので、この季節独特の動きだと捉えればいいと思います。

（10月利上げ観測が再浮上）
・繰り返しになりますが、債券の整理はたぶん終わって、それに充てる株の売りが需給で出て下がった。
・「理由は何だ」とみんながニュースを探しに行って、利上げもその一つなんだと思います。
・ただ、現実的に10月はない、11月だと思います。
・年に1回あるのは仕方ないですし、あと2、3回あるというのは既定路線。
・それは、今日の債券市場を見れば明らかで、それで株が下がったというのは順番がおかしい。
・債券の利回りが前日より低いのをどう説明するんだ、となりますので。
・需給だと思っていればいいと思います。

（GSが債券ロングを推奨？）
・実質金利で言えば、ここ20年近くでいちばん高いんじゃないでしょうか。
・そういう意味では債券を買うというのはまともな推奨だと思います。

（債券買いの株売り？）
・少し戻りますが、9月にこういう動きが出ると思っていたのに出なかった。
・それを需給が案外強いと見るか、10月に持ち越したと見るかでしたが、今から思えば10月に持ち越したと捉えればいいと思います。
・普通に考えれば、今月決算が始まりますし、好決算が結構出ているので、決算が始まって株が下がり続けるのは考えにくい。
・それに中間選挙が終わるというのもある。
・ですので売られるとすればそれまで、つまり今なんです。
・このタイミングまで売られるのは仕方ないけれど、その先もこれが続くというのは非常に考えにくいと私は思います。

（EPS伸び、揺るぎない数字）
・マーケットは地政学リスクや金利、政治など色々なものに振らされますが、究極のところ株式は利益がいちばんの指標です。
・ご指摘のとおり利益がこれだけ上がっていて、株がついていっていない状況なので、あまり弱気になる必要はないと思います。
・もう一つ申し上げると、今年は確かに利益成長率が高いですが、来年も今年の36%がそのまま続くとは考えにくいので、そこは割り引く必要がある。
・それにしても、今年のS&P500指数の上昇率はまだ低いと思いますね。

MARKET UPDATE — THURSDAY, 15 OCTOBER 2026

Hot inflation raised the price of money. And the AI boom, much of it built on borrowed money, flinched.

Data-centre debt cracked, Korea crashed 8%, and bonds became a safe haven again — on the same night TSMC posted the biggest profit in its history.

Today's question isn't whether AI demand is real. It's who can afford to fund it at 5% interest rates.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 THE SPARK: INFLATION RUNS HOTTER

US prices rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% over the year, up from 3.4% and above the 3.6% forecast.

🔸 Petrol jumped 9.1% in a month and caused more than half the rise. Diesel and other fuels are up 61% on the year, heating oil 74%, airfares 22%. The Iran war is the main reason. 

🔸 The worrying part is "core" inflation, which strips out food and energy because they swing wildly. It rose 0.3% (forecast 0.2%) and 2.6% annually (forecast 2.5%). Clothes, toys, used cars, rent and computers all rose — a sign high fuel costs are spreading into everything else. 

🔸 Wages rose only 3% while prices rose 3.7%. 
Put simply: most Americans are getting poorer in real terms, for the sixth month running.

💡 Why it matters: the Federal Reserve (America's central bank) fights inflation by raising interest rates, which makes borrowing more expensive for everyone — from homebuyers to tech giants.

🟢 THE FED: HIKE OR WAIT?

The Fed raised rates last month to 3.75–4.00%, its first hike in three years. Its next decision is on 28 October — six days before the midterm elections.

🔸 Traders' odds of an October hike jumped to about 50% after the data, closed near 37%, and slipped to roughly 25% in Asia this morning (CME FedWatch). 

🔸 San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said more hikes are probably needed, but there is no urgency to move this month. The White House's Kevin Hassett urged the Fed to wait. Most economists expect a hold in October and a hike in December. 

🔸 The Fed's "Beige Book" business survey mentioned high diesel costs 21 times, versus twice last time. Hiring is frozen, prices are climbing — economists called it "stagflationary": weak growth plus rising prices, the toughest combination for any central bank. 

🔸 Mortgage rates hit 7.5%, the highest since November 2023. Home-purchase applications fell 4% in a week.

🟢 THE CRACK: AI'S DEBT PROBLEM

This is where rates and AI collide. Some AI companies are building data centres with huge amounts of borrowed money, betting future profits will repay it. Higher rates make that bet much more expensive.

🔸 CoreWeave, which rents AI computing power and owes nearly $50bn, fell 15% and another 6% after hours — about a fifth of its value gone. Its 2032 bonds now yield over 15%, trading below 80 cents on the dollar. In plain English: lenders now treat it as a risky borrower. Its CEO called markets "irrational". 

🔸 The cost of insuring Oracle, SoftBank and CoreWeave against default rose, in some cases to record levels. 

🔸 Oracle fell 8.8%, Nebius 10%. Dell sank 11.4% and HPE 8.2% after Barclays downgraded both. 

🔸 Chip stocks (SOX index) fell 4.3%, a sixth straight loss — their longest losing run since May 2025 and roughly a 10% drop. Adding pressure: China's CXMT announced progress on advanced memory chips, and on Tuesday Broadcom's CEO compared the AI trade to a casino.

🟢 ANTHROPIC: STILL GROWING, BUT SLOWER

Anthropic (maker of Claude), valued at $965bn and planning a November IPO, told investors that Q3 revenue rose about 46% to $16.8bn (FT).

🔸 Strong — but revenue more than doubled the quarter before. Estimates of yearly revenue run-rate are around $74bn (SemiAnalysis), below summer hopes of $100bn+. 

🔸 Reasons cited: a stronger OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft building their own tools, a price war with cheaper Chinese rivals, and Anthropic cutting back "distillation" (rivals training on its outputs), which had made up 5–7% of revenue. 

🔸 The bull case: it was profitable on an adjusted basis for a second quarter, with $1.70 earned for every $1 spent on computing.

💡 Why it matters: AI labs are the customers paying for chips and data centres. If their growth slows, the whole supply chain gets repriced.

🟢 THE WIPEOUT: ASIA AND THE GLOBE

🔸 South Korea's Kospi plunged about 7.6%, triggering a trading halt — down over 15% this week. Samsung fell 9.9%, SK Hynix about 11%. 

🔸 Japan's Nikkei fell about 5%. SoftBank lost over 9%, Kioxia 11%. China's CSI 300 hit its lowest since August 2025. 

🔸 A hidden risk: Korea and Taiwan now make up almost half the main emerging-markets index, and just TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix about 30% (Goldman Sachs). "Diversifying" into emerging markets is now largely another AI bet. 

🔸 Europe held up, being light on AI. FTSE +0.3%, CAC +0.2%, DAX −0.3%. Food and drink stocks rose 1.7% as investors sought safety; Infineon fell 8%.

🟢 THE TWIST: TSMC'S RECORD QUARTER

In the middle of the panic, TSMC — which makes over 90% of the world's most advanced chips — reported a sixth straight record quarter.

🔸 Net profit rose about 68% to NT$763.1bn (~$23.6bn), beating forecasts of roughly NT$741bn. Revenue rose about 50% to ~$46.7bn. 

🔸 ASML, which makes the machines that make chips, said customers are already seeking orders for 2029–2030.

💡 The real story: the AI money is still flowing. What's being punished is debt, not demand.

🟢 WALL STREET

🔸 S&P 500 −1.1% to 7,718.94 and Nasdaq −1.9% to 26,692.87 — both their worst days since July. The Dow slipped just 0.1% to 51,621.48. 

🔸 The index is still up about 13% this year, but the median stock is up only 4%, and over 200 S&P stocks are negative. A handful of AI giants are carrying the market. 

🔸 Apple rose 0.5%, closing above $5 trillion in value for the first time. 

🔸 Futures: Nasdaq −1.25%, S&P −0.34%, Dow +0.36%. The VIX "fear gauge" is 17.5 — up, but still calm.

🟢 BONDS: THE SAFE HAVEN RETURNS

The 10-year Treasury yield spiked to 5.33% after the inflation data, then reversed sharply as investors fled tech. It now sits near 5.09% (−10bp). The 2-year is 4.73%, the 30-year 5.43%.

💡 Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions. Falling yields mean investors are buying government bonds — a classic "flight to safety". After months of selling bonds, investors are again using them to hedge against falling stocks.

🔸 The dollar index fell 0.6% to 101.95 after hitting its highest level against the euro since May 2025 on Wednesday.

🟢 BANKS & CORPORATE

🔸 Bank of America fell 4.8% (8% at one point) after a $1.2bn anti-money-laundering fine and a profit miss even excluding it. Good sign: loan demand is still growing despite higher rates. Morgan Stanley fell 3% despite higher profit. 

🔸 Netflix is cutting about 1,000 jobs (6% of staff), its largest cuts since 2022, a week before earnings. Shares are down over 40% in a year. 

🔸 Berkshire Hathaway put another $330m into Bending Spoons (owner of Vimeo), which surged 41%.

🟢 OIL & THE IRAN WAR

Brent eased to about $104.67 a barrel and WTI $94.07, partly on US sanctions relief for Russian diesel.

🔸 But Hormuz is getting worse. On 11 October only 2.9m barrels passed through, versus 20.8m on 8 October and a pre-war average of 17.1m a day. The US says it escorted 19m+ barrels on Monday. 

🔸 UKMTO logged 15 attacks on ships since 6 October, 11 of them in four days. Two vessels sank. An Iranian official says the new tactics aim partly to influence the US midterms. 

🔸 CNN reports the US has drawn up plans that could use its largest non-nuclear bomb on Iranian energy and nuclear sites. Trump says the war will end "very soon". 

🔸 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh's airport, prompted travel warnings. The IMF sees Saudi Arabia's economy shrinking 3.3% this year.

💡 Why it matters: about a fifth of the world's oil and LNG normally passes through Hormuz. Every closure feeds petrol prices, then inflation, then interest rates — the chain that started this whole sell-off.

🟢 UKRAINE: A RIFT WITH WASHINGTON

🔸 Ukraine says US intelligence warnings stopped and military Starlink speeds were cut after it refused to halt strikes on Russian refineries. Musk says limits on the military version are set by the US government. Trump denies cutting intelligence. Who ordered the cuts is unconfirmed. 

🔸 Zelensky says refinery strikes will resume: "The block is out." Ukraine's drones have knocked out 40–50% of Russia's refining capacity — so this is upward pressure on diesel prices. 

🔸 The US also floated unfreezing some of Russia's ~€260bn frozen assets to restart peace talks. Europe refused.

🟢 CRYPTO

🔸 Bitcoin $81,149 (−0.5%), Ethereum $2,370 (−2%). 

🔸 Bitcoin held up far better than chip stocks, but higher-rate risk is no friend to crypto. Ethereum, more sensitive to risk appetite, lagged.

🟢 ELSEWHERE

🔸 UK: the economy grew unexpectedly in August. 

🔸 Australia lost 39,300 jobs in September against expectations of a 20,000 gain.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🟢 WHAT IT MEANS

The AI boom has entered its expensive phase. When money was cheap, investors rewarded anyone building AI capacity. At 5% yields, they're asking who can pay the bills.

🔸 The market is now sorting AI winners from AI borrowers. Cash-rich firms like TSMC, ASML and Apple are holding up. Debt-heavy builders like CoreWeave and Oracle are being punished. 

🔸 The bear case: rising rates, slowing AI-lab growth and record concentration mean a small group of stocks now carries the global market. 

🔸 The bull case: AI demand still exceeds supply, there is no recession, and volumes were relatively light. As Julius Baer's Mark Matthews put it, stocks are "not expensive". 

🔸 Today's PPI (wholesale prices) and retail sales will decide whether the Fed feels pressure for an October hike.

What to watch: Hormuz flows, CoreWeave's bonds, and whether today's data confirms or calms Wednesday's inflation scare.

🗓️ CALENDAR

Today (ET): 
🔸 08:30 — PPI (forecast +0.5–0.6% m/m, core +0.3%), retail sales (+0.3% vs 1.2% prior), jobless claims, Empire State and Philadelphia Fed surveys 

🔸 23:30 — Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks (IMF meetings, Bangkok)

Coming up: 
🔸 Next week — Netflix earnings 

🔸 27–28 Oct — Fed meeting 

🔸 3 Nov — US midterm elections 

🔸 November — Anthropic's planned IPO

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💭 THOUGHT FOR THE DAY

"Fall seven times, stand up eight." — Japanese proverb

Markets fall. Markets recover. The investors who last are the ones who learn something every time they get back up.

💬 How can I make these updates better? Suggestions, are always welcome.

Sources: Reuters, Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, The Economist, Al Jazeera English, Bureau of Labor Statistics, CME FedWatch, Kpler, UKMTO, TradingView

Here is a summary of Anthropic’s engineering article, "Building Effective AI Agents":

Overview

Based on insights from working with customers and building agents internally, Anthropic emphasizes that the most successful LLM agent implementations do not rely on complex frameworks, but instead use simple, composable patterns.

1. Key Distinction: Workflows vs. Agents

Workflows: Systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined, deterministic code paths. They offer predictability and consistency.

Agents: Systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks based on environmental feedback.

Guideline: Always start with the simplest solution (often a single LLM call with retrieval) and only increase complexity when it demonstrably improves performance, keeping in mind the trade-offs of latency and cost.

2. Foundational Building Block: The Augmented LLM

The core building block of any agentic system is an LLM enhanced with:

Retrieval (fetching external data)

Tools (executing actions/APIs)

Memory (maintaining state across turns)

3. Common Agentic Workflows

The article outlines five core workflow patterns ranging from low to high complexity:
Prompt Chaining: Decomposing a task into a sequential pipeline where each LLM call processes the output of the previous one (ideal for fixed subtasks like outlining then writing).

Routing: Classifying an input and directing it to a specialized downstream task or model (e.g., routing simple queries to smaller, faster models and complex ones to advanced models).

Parallelization: Running LLMs simultaneously either via sectioning (breaking independent subtasks apart) or voting (running the same task multiple times for consensus/guardrails).

Orchestrator-Workers: A central orchestrator LLM dynamically breaks down open-ended tasks and delegates them to worker LLMs (useful for complex multi-file coding or search tasks).

Evaluator-Optimizer: A loop where one LLM generates a response and another provides iterative feedback/evaluation until criteria are met.

4. Autonomous Agents
When open-ended flexibility is required, agents operate in a loop: they receive a goal, plan steps, execute tools, analyze the "ground truth" feedback from the environment, and adapt.
Best used for: Open-ended problem spaces where fixed paths cannot be hardcoded (e.g., coding/software engineering tasks like solving GitHub issues, customer support resolution).
Caveat: Higher autonomy means higher costs and potential compounding errors, requiring proper sandboxing and guardrails.

5. Best Practices & Frameworks

Frameworks: While SDKs and frameworks help developers get started quickly by handling boilerplate, they can add unnecessary abstractions, obscure prompts, and tempt developers to add unneeded complexity. Developers should start by using LLM APIs directly.

Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Tool definitions should be treated with the same meticulous care as prompts. Tools should be intuitive, self-explanatory, token-efficient, and designed to prevent model errors (e.g., requiring absolute file paths instead of relative ones).

Conclusion
Building effective agentic systems isn't about building the most complex architecture; it's about simplicity, transparency, and careful tool design. Start with simple prompts and workflows, and only scale up to autonomous agents when simpler solutions fall short.

https://t.co/sVciBfeCh7

【7581 サイゼリヤ｜値上げと最高益更新への期待】

サイゼリヤが10月14日に発表した決算と今期業績予想に注目しています。

2026年8月期の売上高は3,014億円、営業利益は164億円。営業利益は前期比5.9%増となりました。

さらに2027年8月期は営業利益212億円、前期比29.1%増を計画。経常利益も208億円と23.6%増加し、4期連続の過去最高益更新を見込んでいます。

■ 価格改定は収益改善の転換点か

今回、特に注目したいのが10月29日から実施される平均6%の値上げです。

ミラノ風ドリアは300円から320円に引き上げられます。

長年、低価格を競争力としてきたサイゼリヤにとって、価格戦略の転換は重要な経営判断です。

値上げ後も客数を維持できれば、原材料費や人件費の上昇を吸収し、利益率の改善につながる可能性があります。

■ 国内外の店舗拡大

今期は国内35店舗、海外86店舗の純増を計画しています。

海外事業の成長に加え、国内では都市部を含む新規出店の採算性が重要になります。

単純な店舗数の拡大ではなく、1店舗当たりの収益力を高められるかがポイントです。

■ 株価への影響

14日の終値は6,550円、前日比3.82%安でした。

好業績予想は取引終了後の発表であり、今後の株価反応を見極める必要があります。

市場では利益成長への期待が高まる一方、値上げによる客離れを懸念する見方も考えられます。

また、前期の営業利益は従来予想を下回っており、直近6～8月期の収益性も悪化しました。

強気の業績予想だけでなく、実際の利益改善を確認することが重要です。

■ 私の見方

サイゼリヤの強みは、手頃な価格と効率的な店舗運営、そして海外展開にあります。

今回の値上げが収益力強化につながれば、今後の企業価値を支える材料になるでしょう。

中長期では前向きに評価していますが、短期的な株価上昇を保証するものではありません。

今後は客数、既存店売上高、営業利益率の3点を重点的に確認したいと思います。

1. 建议每周进行至少 150分钟 的中等强度有氧运动，或 75分钟 的高强度有氧运动。
2. 动起来总比不动强：哪怕是微小的日常活动，也能带来显著的健康益处；对于久坐人群，最显著的健康回报往往来自“从无到有”的迈步。

15日の欧州債券相場は、長期債が主導する形で上昇した。AI投資ブームを巡るリスクへの懸念が再び意識され、安全資産とされる国債への需要が高まった。
ドイツ10年債利回りは5ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp=0.01%）低下し、3.41%で取引を終えた。2年債利回りは2bp低下の3.11%となった。長期債利回りの低下幅が大きく、イールドカーブはブル・フラット化した。

英国債も上昇した。30年債利回りは6bp低下の5.85%、2年債利回りは2bp低下の4.88%となった。

投資家は、バンコクで16日に登壇する米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）のウォーシュ議長の発言を待っている。今週発表された米国の物価関連指標では、インフレ圧力が根強いことが示された。市場は今月後半の米連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）で利上げに踏み切る可能性について、さらなる手掛かりを探ることになる。

英国のFTSE100指数は1.1%上昇し、スイスとフランスの主要株価指数も値上がりした。

From protein LMs that cut pretraining compute instead of adding parameters, to scientific agents that can't release a result until structured validators say yes.

BioTender Daily Papers #80: 6 new papers (arXiv 4 + accepted author manuscripts 2) across 3 directions.

🧬 Protein language models & molecular-optimization benchmarks
• ProtModernBERT: ports recent BERT architecture upgrades to amino-acid pretraining. Abstract reports matching or approaching Amplify-120M and ProtBert with ~80–90% fewer pretraining FLOPs, tested on secondary structure, disorder, subcellular localization, and ProteinGym zero-shot fitness vs ProtBert, Amplify, and ESM2; cluster-split validation and random-init controls separate architecture from data — arXiv preprint; corpus size, fine-tuning budgets, and cross-family extrapolation need a unified protocol
• PMO-Dock: moves molecular-optimization evaluation from simple property oracles to structure-based docking — 25 tasks spanning hit generation, lead optimization, and target selectivity, with validation tasks split from test tasks and a capped test-time oracle budget. Across RL, discrete diffusion, GFlowNets, and LLM evolutionary search, no method wins everywhere and hyperparameter transfer is method-dependent — arXiv preprint; docking scores ≠ real activity or synthesizability

🔬 Single-cell virtual perturbation & combinatorial gene extrapolation
• DKO virtual knockouts: predicts cell-specific knockout effects from unperturbed scRNA-seq, no pre-built GRN or matched perturbation data. Across human, mouse, fly, and worm, predicted responses to the same gene grow more dispersed with age, tracking somatic mutation burden and aging scores — arXiv preprint; model inference, not same-cell measured perturbation, so a testable hypothesis rather than causal proof
• Do perturbation predictors learn gene interactions? Uses "sum of two single-gene effects" as the baseline and defines additive divergence. On 3 Perturb-seq datasets × 8 method families, dedicated neural predictors don't reliably beat the additive baseline, and larger departures from additivity tend to mean larger errors — NeurIPS 2026 ML4Molecules Workshop accepted author manuscript; whether this signal lifts hit rates in closed-loop screens is untested

🌳 Generative phylogenetics & gated scientific agents
• Deep generative phylogenetics: a conditional generative model of the tree posterior, trained with discrete diffusion to build trees top-down, middle-out, or bottom-up, for evolutionary processes whose likelihoods are intractable. Vs Phyloformer 2, MCMC, and IQ-TREE on real + synthetic data, reports more accurate posterior recovery under complex models — NeurIPS 2026 accepted author manuscript; depends on how realistic the simulator is, scale and misspecification robustness still open
• Structure Before Intelligence: defines agent reliability as what gets released — mandatory checks, fault isolation, version tracking, recomputation, and risk gates around the workflow DAG; the LLM can propose fixes but can't bypass validators. On 60 injected-fault instances across 2 workflows, authors report full validation prevents invalid results from being released, risk estimation got similar safety with fewer validators, and the LLM itself added no measurable gain — arXiv preprint, small proof of concept

The common thread:
Honest baselines over bigger claims. Compute-per-performance instead of parameter counts, additive baselines that expose fake "interaction" learning, held-out oracle budgets, and hard release gates that don't depend on a smarter agent.

From efficient protein LMs → docking benchmarks → virtual knockouts + interaction checks → generative trees + gated agents.

🔗 https://t.co/DvfsaK7iFM

#AIforScience #ComputationalBiology #DrugDiscovery

【Muse Spark Open、Mac Studio 2台で動かす816Bモデル】
🧩 Metaが大規模マルチモーダルモデルの重みを公開し、Macでのオンデバイス実行例もあわせて示しました。

■ 1. どんなモデルか
  ▸ 総パラメータは816B、推論時に活性化するのは42Bという構成です。
  ▸ 文脈長は1Mトークンで、テキスト・画像・動画・音声を扱えます。
  ▸ コーディングや、エージェントとして長い手順をこなすタスク向けのモデルとして案内されています。

■ 2. Mac Studio 2台での実演
  ▸ 最新のMLXと、Apple M5 Ultra搭載のMac Studio 2台を組み合わせた構成です。メモリは各最大512GBで、合計約1TBになります。一般的なMac 1台でそのまま動くわけではない点にご注意ください。
  ▸ Muse Codeを使い、iOSアプリ「Ice Cubes」のバグ修正、新機能の追加、ビルドまでを行う様子が紹介されています。
  ▸ DaVinci Resolveでのフレーム確認や縦型の切り抜きも、オンデバイスで実演されています。

■ 3. 使う前に確認したいこと
  ▸ 重みはHugging Faceから入手でき、APIでも提供されています。
  ▸ Muse Model Licenseでは商用利用に条件があります。多くの開発者は無料で使えますが、無制限ではありません。導入前に条文をご確認いただくと安心です。

性能の位置づけにはMeta自身の評価も含まれます。ご自身の用途で確かめながら、落ち着いて見ていくのがよさそうです。

🔗 Meta公式発表

AppleとMetaが協力し、Muse AIモデルをMacコンピュータ上で動作させる
2026年10月15日木曜日 午後1時 EDT 公開
キフ・レスウィング、ジョナサン・ヴァニア
https://t.co/EoZqMzhqLA

ティム・クックとマーク・ザッカーバーグは長年対立してきましたが、ジョン・ターナスがその指揮を執っています。アップルライバル同士は人工知能の共通点を見出しています。
メタそしてAppleは木曜日に、開発者が簡単に実行できるようになる新たなコラボレーションを発表しましたメタのAppleのハイエンドデスクトップコンピュータに搭載された新しいオープンウェイトAIモデル。

両社のコラボレーションの中心であるMuse Spark Openは、Metaによると限定的な商業利用を許可するライセンスのもとでリリースされた最も高性能なオープンウェイトモデルです。これは8160億パラメータを持つモデルで、いわゆる専門家の混合アーキテクチャを用いています。オープンウェイトモデルとして、開発者はインターネットから技術のパラメータや重みをダウンロードし、幅広いハードウェア上でモデルを実行できます。
顧客は2台から4台のMac Studio PCをペアリングし、Muse Sparkを使ってコーディング、動画分析、その他のエージェント的な作業を行うことができます。このモデルはクラウドではなくローカルで動作し、セキュリティ層を加え、ユーザーのコスト削減につながると両社は述べています。
数か月にわたる協力の末に木曜日の発表は、シリコンバレーにおけるAIブームが歴史的な同盟関係を変えたことの兆しです。長年にわたりAppleとMetaは互いを警戒し、公的な提携を避けていましたが、2021年にAppleがデジタル広告企業のターゲティング能力を制限するプライバシー変更を導入したことで関係は底を打った。Metaは2022年初頭に、この変更によりその年の収益が100億ドル削減されると見積もっていました。

AppleとMetaの関係者は、Muse Spark Openとのコラボレーションがより深い関係の始まりかどうかについては明言を控えました。

📷

新しいApple Mac StudioコンピュータとStudio Displayは、2022年3月18日にニューヨーク市マンハッタンの5番街にあるApple Storeで販売開始直後に展示されています。

マイク・シーガー |ロイター

Meta AIの責任者アレクサンドル・ワンはインタビューで、多くの強力なオープンウェイトモデルは大きすぎて大多数のパソコンでは動かないが、AppleのMac Studiosはユーザーに十分なメモリを提供しているため、Muse Spark Openを実用的に動かせると述べました。
この動きは、Metaの再開されたAIへの自信を示す重要な証であり、OpenAIやAnthropicにとっても挑戦となる可能性があります。また、AppleがAIチップ分野での強みを増していることを示す可能性もあります。Nvidia大規模なデータセンターでの普及により、これまでのところ支配的でした。
「私たちはAppleと協力し、Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studiosで初めて最先端のエージェント機能をデスクトップに導入しました。ですから、私たちは本当に楽しみにしています」とワン氏は語りました。開発者は、Appleのシリコンに追加設定なしで、Hugging FaceのようなウェブサイトからAIモデルのバージョンをダウンロードできます。Muse Spark OpenもAppleのハードウェア上でより高速に動作するように調整されており、iPhoneメーカーは自社チップの新たなベンチマークを公開し、MLX AIフレームワークが複数のマシンにオープンソースモデルを分割する能力に関する技術文書を公開しました。
ただしMac Studioは安くなく、このAIモデルは最速のAppleチップとできるだけ多くのメモリを必要とします。
現在、必要なM5 Ultraチップと256GBメモリを搭載したMac Studioは少なくとも10,799ドルの価格です。より高価で512GBのRAMを搭載したバージョンが今月後半にリリースされる予定です。

さらに、ユーザーは複数のマシンを購入する必要があります。
オープンソースでの共通基盤

両社はオープンソースAIで協力しており、ワシントンでは自由な中国モデルがアメリカのAIを弱体化させるのではないかと政治家たちが懸念する中、この問題は論争の的となっています。かつてMetaは古いオープンウェイトのLlamaモデル群にAI戦略を中心としていましたが、その後はWangのリーダーシップのもと、独自のモデル作成に注力しています。Wangは昨年、Metaが彼の前スタートアップ企業Scale AIに140億ドル以上を投資した際にMetaに加わりました。

AppleとMeta(当時Facebookとして知られていた)は10年以上前にiPhone拡張機能で提携していましたが、AppleがiPhoneからシステムレベルのFacebook統合を外してからは、2017年に公にパートナーシップを結んでいません。

「敵対関係の多くは私が会社に入った前から始まっていますが、MetaとAppleの間には長い歴史があります」とワン氏は述べ、協力の理由としてAI研究者で元Appleディレクターのダニエル・グロス氏を挙げました。グロス氏は、元GitHub CEOのナット・フリードマンと共に、昨年ザッカーバーグ氏が自社のAI戦略を抜本的に見直す中で重要な採用者でした。

📷

メタCEO。マーク・ザッカーバーグとアップル社のCEOティム・クック。
ジョン・パットマン |アナドル |アル・ドラゴ |ブルームバーグ |ゲッティイメージズ

彼らの指導者たちも厳しい言葉を交わしています。

クックは先月ターナスが後任となるまでアップルのCEOを務めており、2018年のケンブリッジ・アナリティカ事件の際にザッカーバーグを批判し、「こんな状況にはならなかっただろう」と述べた。クックはMetaがユーザーのプライバシーを侵害しているとしばしば批判していました。

ザッカーバーグはまた、昨年ジョー・ローガンに対し、Appleは「iPhone以来、素晴らしいものを発明していない」と公然と侮辱しています。ザッカーバーグは長い間、MetaがAppleに縛られずに所有できるプラットフォームを見つけようとしてきました。
ハードウェアエンジニアであるTernusは、すでにAppleで製品リリースの際にも変化を始めています。
そしてMetaの開発者たちはAppleの製品に抗えませんでした。同社は今年初めに、スーパーインテリジェンスチームが現地のAIやエージェントを実験するために数百台のMacコンピュータを購入しました。
アップルの複数のパートナー
MetaはAppleと提携した最新のAIモデル開発者です。
2024年、AppleはOpenAIと提携し、ChatGPTをSiriに統合すると発表しましたが、統合は「劇的に期待外れ」でOpenAIのユーザー増加にはつながらなかったと、OpenAIはイーロン・マスクのxAIとの法的紛争の一環として提出した。Appleは7月にOpenAIを営業秘密窃盗の罪で訴えましたが、OpenAIはこれを否定しました。
今年初め、AppleはグーグルApple IntelligenceおよびGoogle CloudのインフラでGeminiモデルを使用することを目的としています。
それでも、AppleのAI戦略は、先月リリースされた新しいSiriが、主要な研究所のチャットボットやエージェントほど高度でないため、投資家や顧客から批判を受けています。

一方、Metaはリーディングラボになることに大きく賭けていますが、競合に追いつくのに苦労しており、そのビジネスはほぼ完全に広告に依存しています。MetaのMuseパーソナルエージェントアプリや、今週初めにリリースされた最新の独自基盤モデルMuse Wonderなど、最近の動きは、新たなAIビジネスチャンスに楽観的な投資家たちの関心をそそらせ始めています。

オープンソースはザッカーバーグのAI戦略の一部であり続けています。8月には、MetaがMuse Glimmerという小型のオープンウェイトAIモデルを発表し、ザッカーバーグは最終的により大きく強力なものをリリースすると約束しました。

Muse Spark Openは独自製品であるMuse Wonderほど高度ではありませんが、ワン氏はより多くのコーダーがアップグレードを促すには十分だと述べています。

「これらは私たちが開発・リリースした中で最も高性能なモデルとは言えません」とワン氏は述べました。「しかし、このモデルを小規模に試してみる企業や開発者は多く、その後利用を拡大していくと考えています。」
